description: Canonical reverse-coverage registry for testable normative clauses. Each row pins one protocol obligation to a stable clause_id, an exact prose anchor, a digest of that section's current text, and the evidence that proves it. It closes the direction vector-registry.json cannot: from prose obligation to executable proof. See spec/v1/zh/conformance/conformance-suite.md section 2.

coverage_scope.rule: This registry covers the high-risk observable obligation set named in included_categories. It is deliberately not a numbering of every normative sentence under spec/v1/zh; mechanically numbering prose would manufacture meaningless MUSTs. A green release gate proves that every registered clause has live evidence and that no registered section changed without review. It does NOT prove that every MUST in the specification is registered.
coverage_scope.extension_rule: Adding a normative obligation inside an included category requires adding or updating a clause in the same change. Because section_digest pins the current text of every registered anchor, editing a registered section fails the release gate until the clause and its evidence are re-reviewed.

registry_rules: clause_id values are stable and MUST NOT be reused after a clause is retired; retire a clause by setting status=deprecated instead of deleting the row.
source_anchor MUST be a repository-relative markdown path plus an existing heading slug. section_digest MUST equal the sha256 of that heading's section text as computed by tools/lint_artifacts.py.

testability_grade=vector rows MUST list evidence_refs containing active vector ids from vector-registry.json. testability_grade=api_shape or audit rows MUST instead declare test_plan describing the non-vector proof.
A clause MUST NOT claim evidence it does not have: an obligation with no executable proof stays out of this registry rather than pointing at an unrelated vector.

clauses.requirement: Canonical JSON serialization (key order, number form, NFC strings, duplicate-key rejection) is the single encoding used for every digest, signature and canonical comparison.
Digest suite identifiers, canonical event digest computation and the bytewise tie-break order are fixed; implementations MUST NOT substitute another hash encoding or comparison direction.

The signature carrier MUST cryptographically protect its algorithm selection, and the binding payload MUST bind domain and audience; a signature valid for one algorithm, domain or audience MUST NOT verify for another.

HLC well-formedness, logical-counter overflow handling and the causal-first usage boundary: HLC breaks ties between causally incomparable items only and MUST NOT select a winner in shared protocol state.
Cursors are opaque server-issued tokens bound to their query scope; clients MUST NOT parse or forge them and cross-scope replay MUST be rejected.
Encrypted envelopes carry a pre-encryption immutable header; AAD digest and ciphertext digest are computed over fixed transcripts and any mismatch MUST fail closed.
Transport encoding bounds: Content-Encoding is forbidden on non-streaming JSON operations and every size limit MUST be enforced before the body is fully buffered or parsed.
Every operation_id ends with <kind>.<action> drawn from the closed kind set, and the action MUST describe a protocol effect rather than an HTTP method name.
clauses.test_plan: Enforced mechanically by tools/lint_artifacts.py: every operation_id in operation-registry.json is checked against the closed kind set and against forbidden HTTP-method action names. There is no runtime vector because the obligation is on the published contract, not on request handling.

clauses.requirement: Every write operation declares a machine-readable idempotency mechanism and retry safety; clients MUST NOT be left to guess the recovery path of an uncertain outcome.
Protected current-v1 endpoints require sender-constrained proof of possession; a bare bearer session grant MUST NOT authenticate a protected request.

MLS integration boundary: only registered active ciphersuites reach the wire, Welcome and KeyPackage binding is verified byte-exactly, encryption floors MUST NOT be downgraded, an encrypted envelope MUST NOT disclose an AAD event id wider than the Realm aad_visibility ceiling, every MLS epoch MUST bind the independently re-derived security frontier for its accepted key-access state, and epoch-0 leaf indices MUST be recovered only from digest-verified RFC 9420 GroupInfo/ratchet-tree bytes committed by the accepted genesis.
Read-trigger expiry anchors derive from anonymous aggregate contributions, converge under replay and reordering, and MUST NOT reveal reader identity or reader counts.
Directory resolution failures are indistinguishable: unauthorized, non-existent and policy-denied targets MUST NOT be separable by error code, field set or timing.

A Control Move MUST carry a CBA basis covered by an accepted Seal except in the two closed anchor-unit contexts; same-batch events MUST NOT advance their own authorization basis, and basis-free anchor Events remain Control Moves with proposal receipts and pending-index obligations.

Seal canonical bytes exclude self-reference and DataEvent digests, compaction preserves control roots, Realm reducer selection comes from the authenticated singleton control cell, and equivocating notaries are quarantined instead of silently merged.

A grant stays within the union of the authorities its issuer_authority_refs name and within their per-action validity window; cycles over grant refs and inactive refs MUST fail closed rather than widen the effective permission set.
Revocation rolls back downstream grants and forces a re-check of dependent decisions; a revoked grant MUST NOT keep authorizing pending or cached writes.
Lattice joins are idempotent, commutative and associative per family; data-plane conflicts return structured bottom instead of electing a winner by arrival order or HLC.
Field patches apply atomically against the declared pre-state; a partially applied patch or an unbound pre-state MUST be rejected.
Every reducer-input event kind declares a closed cell contract (cell family, subject, lattice, bottom, effect projection); an unregistered projection MUST NOT be improvised.
Call state transitions follow the registered matrix, terminal states are absorbing, replaying the same state is a no-op, and concurrent siblings resolve to bottom.
Invite claim is a state machine: a consumed token MUST NOT be re-subjected, expiry uses canonical time, and the membership transition is atomic with the claim.

Account Data keys are server-versioned compare-and-set registers: a stale write MUST fail with cas_conflict, the revision high-water mark never goes backwards, and domain merge runs client-side on plaintext.
Multi-device read cursor merge is causal-first: a causally dominating position wins regardless of HLC, HLC decides only concurrent positions, and device_id only breaks equal HLCs.
To-device delivery executes each durable handler effect exactly once: redelivery is deduplicated by sender-scoped message id and queue removal happens only on explicit ack.
Member delivery binding never silently downgrades: a stale binding frontier, an expired handover grace window or an unresolvable binding MUST fail closed instead of routing to the previous service.

A revoked authorization observed inside the configured freshness window remains deterministically accepted-but-stale for reducer input; a deployment may hide it locally but MUST NOT reject it from the canonical join.
Every accountable principal on an Actor Event must have an active matching accountability grant; any missing grant rejects the whole Event without a stripped projection.

Realm proposal configuration must leave a realizable decision schedule: decision window does not exceed the absolute deadline, equality is valid only when deferral is disabled, and invalid create/update writes reject without state change.
Optional nullable fields normalize absent and null unless a conditional branch requires the field or x-arkret-presence-semantics=distinct explicitly assigns three business states.
clauses.test_plan: tools/gen_property_presence_manifest.py must classify every tristate audit target with zero unresolved dispositions; the Rust SDK draft202012_runtime and Circle payload tests pin the sole distinct target and its Missing/Null/Value round-trip.

clauses.requirement: An accepted closed-anchor Control Move, its proposal receipt and pending index are committed atomically; the covering Seal atomically applies lineage and cell effects and marks every covered pending digest sealed, rolling back if any digest is absent.

Fields inside the event_digest preimage MUST NOT commit to the enclosing Event's own event_id or event_digest, nor to the event_id or envelope digest of a not-yet-formed sibling Event in the same atomic unit or ordered submit batch; such a commitment has no fixed point and MUST be rejected as event_id_digest_mismatch. Commitments of that kind MUST instead use the counterpart's payload digest or a structure outside the preimage (proofs, receipts).
